summary: Defines the Network Control Protocols for establishing and configuring SNA over PPP and SNA over LLC 802.2 over PPP, letting IBM-style networks run across PPP links.

eli5.summary: This lets an old kind of corporate network talk across a regular phone-line style connection.

questions: how does sna run over ppp
what ppp protocol number is used for sna
subtitle: How IBM's SNA networking traffic is carried and configured over a PPP link.

tldr.problem: PPP needs a Network Control Protocol for each network-layer protocol it carries, and IBM's Systems Network Architecture (SNA) did not have one.
tldr.mechanism: SNACP reuses the LCP packet exchange with a few changes, in two separate and independent variants: one for SNA over LLC 802.2 and one for SNA without it. It then carries one SNA message unit per PPP frame.
tldr.outcome: SNA can run over point-to-point links; the SNACP itself has no configuration options and the memo says nothing about security.

today: RFC 2043 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on PPP as defined in RFC 1661.

sections.title: PPP and the Need for SNACP
sections.content:
The Point-to-Point Protocol (RFC 1661) has three main parts: a method for encapsulating multi-protocol datagrams, a Link Control Protocol (LCP) for establishing, configuring and testing the link, and a family of Network Control Protocols (NCPs) for configuring each network-layer protocol.

Both ends first use LCP to set up the link. Then PPP must send SNACP packets to choose and configure the SNA network-layer protocol. Once SNACP reaches the Opened state, SNA datagrams can flow. The link stays configured until LCP or SNACP packets close it, or until an external event such as an inactivity timer or administrator intervention.
sections.eli5: First the two ends agree how the link works. Then they agree on the rules for SNA. Only then can SNA messages travel.

sections.title: SNA Terminology
sections.content:
The RFC uses the usual RFC 2119 style words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD and MAY, and defines several SNA terms.

  • PIU (path information unit): a transmission header (TH) alone, or a TH followed by a basic information unit (BIU) or a BIU segment. It is analogous to a datagram.
  • TH: control information created by path control to route message units and control their flow.
  • BIU: the unit passed between half-sessions, a request/response header followed by a request/response unit.
  • NLP (Network Layer Packet): in High Performance Routing (HPR), the message unit that carries data over the route. It is also analogous to a datagram.
sections.eli5: SNA has its own words for a message, such as PIU and NLP. They mean roughly the same as a packet of data.

sections.title: The SNA Control Protocol
sections.content:
SNACP configures, enables and disables SNA on both ends of the link. It uses the same packet exchange mechanism as LCP, and the RFC says it is exactly the same as LCP except for a few points. There are actually two SNA NCPs, one for SNA over LLC 802.2 and one for SNA without LLC 802.2. They are negotiated separately and independently.

The differences from LCP are as follows.

  • Frame modifications: packets may use any frame format changes negotiated during link establishment.
  • Protocol field: exactly one SNACP packet goes in the PPP Information field. The text of section 2 gives the Protocol field as hex 804B (SNA over LLC 802.2) or hex 804D (SNA).
  • Codes: only Codes 1 through 7 are used (Configure-Request, Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, Configure-Reject, Terminate-Request, Terminate-Ack and Code-Reject). Other codes are treated as unrecognized and get a Code-Reject.
  • Timeouts: an implementation should be prepared to wait for authentication and link quality determination before timing out on a Configure-Ack. It is suggested that it give up only after user intervention or a configurable amount of time.
  • Options: there are no Configuration Options for either SNA variant.

SNACP packets may not be exchanged until PPP reaches the Network-Layer Protocol phase, and packets that arrive earlier should be silently discarded.
sections.eli5: The rules for setting up SNA are copied from the rules for setting up the link, with a few changes. There are two sets, one for each flavour of SNA, and they work separately.

sections.title: Sending SNA Over PPP
sections.content:
Before any SNA packet is sent, PPP must reach the Network-Layer Protocol phase and the right SNACP must be in the Opened state. The maximum length of an SNA packet is the same as the maximum length of the PPP Information field.

For SNA XID or FID2 PIUs over LLC, exactly one PIU goes in the PPP Information field, with the PPP Protocol field set to hex 004B. The frame carries the Protocol field, then DSAP address, SSAP address, Control field and the LLC Information field holding the PIU. LLC(2) is included for link-level error recovery, which is done by the routers at each end.

For HPR, exactly one Network Layer Packet goes in the Information field, with Protocol field hex 004D. The frame holds the Protocol field, NHDR, THDR and data.

It is architecturally possible to carry HPR NLPs over LLC over PPP using type 004B, if the optional HPR link-level error recovery tower is implemented.
sections.eli5: Each PPP envelope holds exactly one SNA message. The label on the envelope tells the other end which of the two kinds of SNA it is.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC contains a single statement on security: security issues are not discussed in this memo. Anything about authentication happens in PPP itself, which SNACP only waits for before it times out.
sections.eli5: This document does not say anything about keeping SNA safe from snoopers.
